subject.name_or_desc: William Laud, Archbishop of Canterbury (the quesited), then a prisoner

context.question: What manner of death should Canterbury die?
context.setting: The Archbishop was imprisoned and his fate in question during the Civil War; Lilly professes he honoured the man and never had speech or acquaintance with him.

attachments.key_positions: The cusp of the ninth house taken for his Ascendant (he being a man of the Church); Saturn, lord of that sign, in his fall, a long time retrograde, and posited in the twelfth of the figure; the Moon separating from Saturn and applying to the Sun neer the cusp of the eighth house; the Sun in a fiery sign applying to an opposition of Mars, the dispositor of the aged Bishop; Mars in an airy and humane sign; the Moon wanting seven degrees of the body of Mars
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; the ascending degree is not given in the prose and is not asserted here.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. LXXII: what manner of death Canterbury should die (printed pp.419–420)
